new_value: Mark 2026-11-23: the announcement is an invitation; liveness comes from joining the call room, and an ended message is advisory.

{"id":"mimid-1wgh.117","title":"Decision: a call announcement is an invitation, not a liveness indicator","description":"Mark decided 2026-11-23, following decision mimid-1wgh.116, for bead
mimid-1wgh.114.1.

THE QUESTION. The announcement message carries the call room's URI
(decision mimid-1wgh.116). Nothing then tells the chat that the call
ended, so a client that read the announcement shows "call in progress"
forever.

WHAT MAKES IT HARD, and it decides the answer: the people who most need
to know cannot see it. A client that JOINED the call is in the call room
and watches its membership shrink, so it knows. A client that only read
the announcement is in the PARENT chat, not the call room, and MIMI gives
a non-member no way to ask who is in a room -- deliberately. The agent
cannot answer it either: it is not a member of the call's group. So
liveness is not knowable remotely without a heartbeat.

OPTIONS WEIGHED:
(a) The announcement is an INVITATION, not a live indicator. Liveness
    comes from joining the call room and looking. An "ended" message is
    sent when it can be and is advisory.
(b) An explicit "ended" announcement, treated as authoritative.
(c) An expiry in the announcement ("live until T") that the caller
    refreshes while the call runs.

CHOSEN: (a).

WHY:
- It is the only option that does not claim knowledge it cannot have. A
  client showing a live indicator from the chat message alone is showing
  something it cannot actually know, which is a bug that looks like a
  feature.
- (b) is wrong exactly when it matters. The ending message is lost when
  the sender crashes or loses the network, which is the same event that
  ends calls abruptly, so the failure correlates with the case.
- (c) heals itself but pays in noise: a refresh is a message, and every
  client that does not understand the extension key renders it, so a long
  call litters the chat with announcements. The cost lands on exactly the
  clients the announcement exists to serve.
- Joining the call room to find out is cheap: it is an MLS group join,
  and a participant of the parent is entitled to it (and would be
  entitled to it without an invite under
  ietf-wg-mimi/mimi-room-policy#45's canJoinFromParent).

WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE BUILD:
- The announcement's text is about a call having been started, and front
  ends render it as an invitation or a chat event, NOT as a live badge.
- An "ended" announcement is worth sending when the agent can tell (the
  call room emptied, or the user hung up) because it makes the chat line
  read sensibly, and it carries no guarantee. Its absence means "not
  known", never "still going".
- No heartbeat, no refresh, no presence. mimid carries no presence
  anywhere (docs/design/agent-frontends.md says so of IRC's MONITOR and
  away-notify) and this does not introduce the first one.

NOT DECIDED HERE: the exact map entry an "ended" announcement uses, which
belongs with the rest of the value's shape in bead mimid-1wgh.114.1.

new_value: {"notes":"SCOPE, added 2026-11-23 after reading draft-atwood-jmap-vtc (decision mimid-1wgh.118): this decision is about the CROSS-PROVIDER CHAT ANNOUNCEMENT, not a claim that mimid never models call state. The VTC draft's state machine is server-enforced and authoritative (\"active\" -\u003e \"ended\" on \"All participants leave or a moderator ends the call\", \"ended\" terminal), and it is right for a PARTICIPANT, whose agent is a member of the call room and sees its membership. What is not knowable is the state of a call the agent never joined: it is not in that room, so it has only what the announcement said. The surface must not present such a state as though it were observed."}
